THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
ORDER Heard Sri.Kushal N.K., learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.

2. This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., with the following prayer:
"To allow the petition and grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 and petitioner No.2/accused No.2 in event of their arrest in Crime No. 19/2023 registered by Chittakula Police Station for P/u/sec. 406, 408, 409, 418, 419, 420,
468, 471 R/w 34 of IPC."

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
3.1 Sri.B.B.Rane, Chairman of Ashray Co-operative Credit Society Limited, Karwar lodged a complaint with Chittakula police, Sadashivgad, Karwar stating that the petitioner No.1 was working as a manger in the said co- operative society and had lent loan to general public and to his wife without proper security and thereby committed criminal breach of trust and sought for action.

After registering the case in Crime No.19/2023 on 03.04.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 408, 409, 418, 419, 420, 468, 471 read with 34 of IPC, police are investigating the matter.
Despite best efforts, the police are unable to apprehend the present petitioners.
4. The attempt made by the petitioners to obtain an order of grant of bail was turned down by the learned District Judge in Crl.Misc. No.122/2023 by order dated 26.04.2023.
Thereafter, the petitioners are before this Court.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri.Kushal N.K., learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that even assuming that the entire allegations against the petitioners stands proved it can only be an irregularity and not illegality as the manager had power to lend loan and therefore the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail.

6. He also pointed out that the petitioners are innocent and they have been made as a scapegoat for illegality said to have been committed by the other officials in the bank and therefore sought for grant of anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail petition by contending that the petitioner No.1 has gone to the extent of lending loan to his own wife without verification of proper material on record and without obtaining necessary security, which is against the norms of the society and therefore prima facie materials would go to show that the petitioners are guilty of the offences alleged against them and therefore sought for rejection of petition.
8.
She also points out that if the petitioners are enlarged on bail, they may not be available for investigation and trial and sought for rejection of bail.
9. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court has perused the material on record meticulously.
10. On such perusal, it is seen that there is no dispute that petitioner No.1 was the manager of Ashray Co-operative Credit Society Limited.
Admittedly, he has lent loans without taking proper security.

Whether at all the petitioners are guilty of the offences alleged against them or not and that they have misappropriated the funds of the society resulting in criminal breach of trust cannot be decided by this Court at this stage by holding a mini trial.
11. It is for the investigating agency to collect such materials to proceed against the petitioners in pursuance of the complaint averments.
Since the petitioners are not available to the investigating agency, the investigation is crippled to a considerable extent.

12. Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that if the petitioners are directed to join the investigation by appearing before the investigating officer and undergo limited period of custodial interrogation, ends of justice would be met.

13. Accordingly, following order is passed:
Sri Nilesh C Naik S/O Dulaba Naik vs The State Of Karnataka on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164216562/
3 ORDER

sentences.text:
The criminal petition is allowed subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioners are directed to join the investigation by appearing before the Investigating Officer on 28.06.2023 at 10.00 a.m.
2.

The Investigating Officer is at liberty to take the petitioners to custody and complete the custodial interrogation, if any, on the same day before 6.00 p.m. and thereafter enlarge the petitioners on bail by taking a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees one lakh only) each with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
3.
The petitioners shall co
- operate with the Investigating Agency in all aspects of the matter.
4. The petitioners shall attend the Court regularly.

5. The petitioners shall mark their attendance before the Investigating Officer on every 3rd Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m., till the final report is filed.
6.
The petitioners shall not directly or indirectly tamper the prosecution evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner.
Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of bail.
Ordered accordingly.
